message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, but you can quickly check your own speed with a few simple steps. Below are a couple of options—pick the one that feels easiest for you.

---

## 1️⃣ Quick “Download‑a‑File” Test (PowerShell)

If you’re on Windows and have PowerShell available, you can download a known‑size file and measure how long it takes. That gives you a rough idea of your download speed.

```powershell
# Create a temp folder if it doesn’t exist
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$env:TEMP\SpeedTest" -Force | Out-Null

# Measure the time it takes to download a 100 MB file
$time = Measure-Command {
    (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile(
        'https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin',
        "$env:TEMP\SpeedTest\100MB.bin"
    )
}

# Convert the elapsed time to seconds and calculate Mbps
$seconds = $time.TotalSeconds
$megabytes = 100
$megabits = $megabytes * 8
$mbps = [math]::Round($megabits / $seconds, 2)

Write-Host "Download took $seconds seconds."
Write-Host "Approximate speed: $mbps Mbps"
```

**What to expect**

- The script downloads a 100 MB file from Hetzner’s public speed‑test server.
- It prints the elapsed time and converts that into megabits per second (Mbps).
- Keep in mind that this is a *single* download test; real‑world speeds can vary with other traffic, server load, etc.

---

## 2️⃣ Use the Official Speedtest CLI (if you have Python)

If you have Python installed, you can use the official Speedtest CLI from Ookla. It’s more accurate because it talks to the same servers that the Speedtest app uses.

### Install (if you haven’t already)

```bash
pip install speedtest-cli
```

### Run a test

```bash
speedtest
```

The output will look something like:

```
Testing from Your ISP (Your City)...
Retrieving speedtest.net configuration...
Testing download speed........................................
Testing upload speed..........................................
Download:  85.23 Mbit/s
Upload:    12.45 Mbit/s
Ping:      23.4 ms
```

**Why this is better**

- It automatically selects the nearest server.
- It measures both download and upload speeds, plus ping.
- It’s the same tool used by the Speedtest app and website.

---

## 3️⃣ Browser‑Based Test

If you prefer not to use the command line, just open a browser and go to:

- <https://www.speedtest.net>
- <https://fast.com> (Netflix’s quick test)
- <https://www.google.com/search?q=speed+test> (Google’s built‑in test)

Click “Go” or “Start” and let it run. It will give you download, upload, and ping metrics.

---

### Quick Summary

| Method | What it measures | How to run |
|--------|------------------|------------|
| PowerShell script | Single download of 100 MB | Copy‑paste the script above |
| Speedtest CLI | Download, upload, ping | `pip install speedtest-cli` → `speedtest` |
| Browser test | Download, upload, ping | Visit speedtest.net or fast.com |

Pick whichever feels most convenient. If you run into any issues (e.g., “command not found” or “pip not installed”), let me know and I can walk you through troubleshooting!
